universities.name: University of Malaya
universities.description: Malaysia's oldest university and consistently its highest-ranked, with roots going back to 1905 (founded in Singapore as the King Edward VII College of Medicine; renamed University of Malaya in 1949 and recognised as a public university in Malaya from 1962). Based in Kuala Lumpur, UM offers a wide range of programmes across multiple faculties. Its International Channel accepts the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) for most undergraduate programmes, and recognised bachelor's degrees for postgraduate study.

admissionRequirements.undergraduate: Completion of 12 years of schooling with a Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC), accepted for most programmes through UM's International Channel. Minimum marks and subjects are set per programme (for example, Engineering: 65% average with at least 60% in Mathematics and Physics; Business Administration: about 70% average). Qualifications graded on a different scale are assessed by UM through a cross-matching process. Medicine does not list the HSC as a direct entry route (accepted routes include A-Level, IB and Foundation/Matriculation). Meeting the requirements makes you eligible to apply; it does not guarantee admission.
admissionRequirements.postgraduate: Recognised Bachelor's degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.00 (or equivalent). Some programmes consider a CGPA of 2.50–2.99 if extra criteria are met (for example an interview, relevant work experience or publications). Degrees from foreign institutions must be recognised in the Malaysian Qualifications Register. Requirements vary by programme and admission is not guaranteed.

tuitionFees.undergraduate: RM 60,900 – RM 149,200 total programme fee for most programmes (international, 2025/26); Pharmacy RM 280,100, Dentistry RM 655,000, Medicine RM 673,200. UM quotes fees for the whole programme, not per year.
tuitionFees.postgraduate: Master's coursework mostly RM 25,000 – RM 80,000 total; PhD roughly RM 50,000 – RM 100,000 total (international, 2025/26). UM quotes fees for the whole programme, not per year.

universities.scholarships: UM Scholarship Scheme (UMSS) and Graduate Research Assistantship Scheme (GRAS/iGRAS) for Master's and PhD research students (postgraduate only); PTE x Universiti Malaya Scholarship (£3,000 towards tuition for international students). The Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) is a Malaysian government postgraduate scheme for selected countries, not a UM scholarship; check whether Bangladesh is eligible.

courses.name: Medicine
courses.tuitionFee: RM 673,200 total programme fee (international, 2025/26)
courses.entryRequirements: UM does not list the HSC as a direct entry route for international applicants. Accepted routes include A-Level (grade A in Biology and Chemistry, and A in Physics or Mathematics), IB (36 points) or Foundation/Matriculation (CGPA 3.80/4.00). An admission test score (MSAT/BMAT/MCAT/GAMSAT) and an interview are required.

universities.name: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia
universities.description: Malaysia's national university, founded on 18 May 1970 (it began in Kuala Lumpur and moved to its main campus in Bangi, Selangor, in 1977). A leading public research university offering programmes across sciences, engineering, medicine, law, and social sciences. Its UKM International (UKMi) route accepts the Bangladeshi Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) for undergraduate study, and recognised bachelor's degrees for postgraduate study.

admissionRequirements.undergraduate: Completion of 12 years of schooling with a Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC), applied through UKM International (UKMi). UKM sets a minimum HSC percentage by country: for Bangladesh it is 80% for most programmes (Engineering, IT, Science, Law, Education, Business) and 85% for Medicine and Dentistry. Required subjects vary by faculty (for example Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry/Biology for Engineering and IT; Biology, Chemistry and Mathematics/Physics for Medicine). An interview may be required. UKM does not state a GPA equivalent on its pages, so check how your HSC result converts. Meeting the requirements makes you eligible to apply; it does not guarantee admission.
admissionRequirements.postgraduate: Recognised Bachelor's degree with a good CGPA from an institution recognised by the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) or accredited by a recognised foreign body; further requirements are set by each faculty or institute. Admission is not guaranteed.

englishRequirements.toefl: 35 - 93 iBT (varies by faculty; HEET also accepted)

tuitionFees.undergraduate: RM 59,920 – RM 90,820 total programme fee for most programmes (UKMi international fee schedule 2024/25); Medicine RM 552,520 total. UKM quotes fees for the whole programme, and a 6% Sales and Service Tax is added for international students.
tuitionFees.postgraduate: Master's roughly RM 28,000 – RM 40,000 total (for example Master of Laws RM 31,910); PhD about RM 71,820 total (Faculty of Law, minimum 8 semesters). Fees vary by faculty and mode of study.

universities.scholarships: Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) and Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP) are Malaysian government postgraduate schemes that UKM supports (eligibility depends on your country); UKM Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) and the UKM Zamalah Scheme support Master's and PhD research students, including international students; Dermasiswa financial aid is for students from low and lower-middle-income countries.
